title: Common definitions for AI Grandma configuration files
description: Reusable $defs shared by all rule-type schemas. These definitions encode shared concepts: meta information, i18n text (multilingual with English as source and fallback), language codes, slot/level/module ids, condition expressions with three-valued (Kleene) logic, etc.

i18n_text.description: Multilingual text object. English (en) is the source text and is required. Other languages (zh, ms, ta) are optional translations. When a translation is missing, the system falls back to English. Non-English medical text must be reviewed by a native speaker or clinician before it can be considered reliable.

language_code.description: Supported language codes: en (English, default), zh (Simplified Chinese), ms (Malay), ta (Tamil).

module_id.description: Four triage modules plus the reserved 'core' module id used by the cross-module screening question set (core_questions.yaml).

versions.description: Version numbers for all configuration bundles used in a session. All fields are optional because different events involve different bundles. Recorded in every event log entry for audit and shadow-mode replay.

value.description: The extracted value. Required when status is 'answered'. The type must match the slot definition in slots.yaml (checked by the downstream validation script).

slot_value.description: A single extracted slot with its status and value. When status is 'answered', value must be present. The value type must conform to the slot's type in slots.yaml (cross-file check by validation script).

session_id.description: Randomly generated session identifier. MUST NOT be derived from any personal information.

outcome_link_key.description: Anonymous key for linking a session to a follow-up outcome record. MUST NOT be derived from any personal information.

condition.description: A recursive condition expression evaluated under three-valued logic. Each predicate produces true / false / unknown. When the referenced slot's status is unknown, declined, or not_asked, the predicate result is unknown — UNLESS the operator itself is is_unknown, is_answered, or is_declined (which always produce true/false). all_of / any_of / not combine results using Kleene logic: unknown AND false = false; unknown AND true = unknown; unknown OR true = true; unknown OR false = unknown; NOT unknown = unknown. Each rule file declares how it handles unknown results (e.g. on_unknown field in redflag rules, uncertainty_policy in decision tables).
